reason: conditional5 passes the registered development point-estimate gates against candidate5; candidate5 also passes against fixed20. conditional5 and repeated-cache both reduce actual external calls from 3 to 2 per request (33.333%), and retrieval calls by 50%. Unequal arm sizes (8 versus 16 requests) are normalized per request rather than rewarding repeated traffic for a larger raw count. With call savings tied, conditional5 has lower measured mean retrieval latency (331.875ms versus 368.75ms) and the larger paired mean latency reduction (60.978% versus 55.789%). Select only the existing conditional5 arm; do not add cache or deduplication. This is development candidate eligibility on four independent questions, not formal noninferiority or evidence to change production defaults.
rankingRule: Quality gates first; actual external call reduction per request first, then measured mean retrieval latency; no failures counted as acceleration. Report raw call counts alongside normalized comparisons.
